meta.description: Five characterization systems — lenses for classifying and comparing government-wide administrative systems — transcribed from the Government element note. Concepts carry their Concept Critique; dimensions carry their Value Set where the characterization framework states one.

systems.name: administrative-system
systems.title: Administrative System
systems.description: Core concepts of public administration as an administrative system: what it is, what it is made of, and what it can do.

entries.name: Public Administration
entries.description: The institutions, organizations, personnel, processes, and activities through which public policies and legal mandates are administered and public affairs are managed.
entries.critique: Public administration is broader than civil service and includes functions beyond the implementation of public services.

entries.name: Government Administration
entries.description: The administrative arrangements and organized activities through which government institutions execute their responsibilities and manage public affairs.
entries.critique: The term may refer to administration across government or, more narrowly, to the administrative apparatus of the executive. Its scope must be specified.

entries.name: Administrative Institution
entries.description: An institution established or recognized to exercise administrative authority, perform administrative functions, or govern administrative conduct.
entries.critique: An administrative institution is not necessarily identical to a single administrative organization.

entries.name: Administrative Organization
entries.description: An organized entity or organizational unit responsible for performing administrative functions under an assigned mandate.
entries.critique: Organizational status, legal personality, and decision-making autonomy vary.

entries.name: Administrative Structure
entries.description: The arrangement of administrative institutions, agencies, departments, organizational units, offices, and their hierarchical or functional relationships.
entries.critique: Formal structure alone does not explain operational processes, capacity, or actual patterns of coordination.

entries.name: Administrative Capacity
entries.description: The ability of public administrative institutions to perform assigned functions, mobilize resources, exercise authority, and achieve intended results.
entries.critique: Capacity is multidimensional; formal staffing and budgets alone do not establish effective capability.

entries.name: Administrative Capability
entries.description: A specific ability of an administrative actor or organization to perform a function or execute an operation under defined conditions.
entries.critique: Capability should be distinguished from available resources, realized performance, and overall institutional capacity.

entries.name: Administrative Autonomy
entries.description: The degree to which an administrative organization can make decisions within its mandate without requiring authorization from another authority.
entries.critique: Autonomy is multidimensional and remains bounded by law, oversight, and accountability.

entries.name: Administrative Discretion
entries.description: The scope of choice available to administrative authorities when interpreting and applying legal mandates or selecting operational alternatives.
entries.critique: The scope of discretion depends on applicable law and is distinct from unrestricted decision-making authority.

systems.name: gov-wide-architecture
systems.title: Government-Wide Administrative Architecture
systems.description: Scope, structure, framework, functions, services, authorities, and coordination of administration across government as a whole.

entries.name: Government-Wide Administrative System
entries.description: The interconnected administrative institutions, organizations, personnel, processes, resources, and relationships through which administrative functions are performed across government as a whole.
entries.critique: Its boundaries must specify which institutions, public entities, and levels of government are included.

entries.name: Government-Wide Administrative Structure
entries.description: The configuration of administrative organizations and units across government, including their hierarchical, functional, and coordinating relationships.
entries.critique: It represents organizational arrangements rather than the entirety of administrative processes and capabilities.

entries.name: Government-Wide Administrative Framework
entries.description: The cross-government legal, institutional, organizational, and procedural arrangements that establish common administrative rules and operating conditions.
entries.critique: A framework establishes shared arrangements but does not necessarily constitute a unified operational system.

entries.name: Government-Wide Administrative Function
entries.description: An administrative function performed across multiple governmental organizations or established centrally to support government as a whole.
entries.critique: Cross-government scope does not necessarily mean centralized execution.

entries.name: Shared Administrative Service
entries.description: An administrative service provided centrally or jointly to multiple public organizations, such as payroll, procurement support, or information technology.
entries.critique: Shared services are one possible operating arrangement, not a defining requirement of government-wide administration.

entries.name: Central Administrative Authority
entries.description: An authority responsible for establishing, coordinating, supervising, or administering specified arrangements across multiple public organizations.
entries.critique: Its powers may be advisory, regulatory, supervisory, or executive and should be specified individually.

entries.name: Interorganizational Coordination
entries.description: The alignment of activities, decisions, responsibilities, or resources across distinct administrative organizations.
entries.critique: Coordination mechanisms may be hierarchical, contractual, procedural, or network-based.

entries.name: Whole-of-Government Approach
entries.description: An approach that seeks to coordinate institutions, policies, resources, or operations across governmental boundaries to address shared objectives.
entries.critique: The approach does not necessarily require organizational integration or centralized control.

systems.name: org-administration
systems.title: Public Organization Administration
systems.description: Organization-specific administration: the internal systems, structures, functions, processes, and controls of one public organization.

entries.name: Public Organization-Specific Administrative System
entries.description: The configuration of personnel, processes, resources, information, rules, and relationships through which a particular public organization performs its administrative and managerial functions.
entries.critique: Its scope is bounded by the organization being examined and should be distinguished from the government-wide administrative system in which it operates.

entries.name: Public Organization-Specific Administrative Structure
entries.description: The internal arrangement of administrative units, offices, positions, authority relationships, and reporting lines within a particular public organization.
entries.critique: It describes internal organizational arrangements rather than the entire administrative system or its operational performance.

entries.name: Internal Administrative Function
entries.description: An administrative function performed within a particular public organization to support its mandate, management, or operations.
entries.critique: Internal functions may rely on shared services or external providers and are not necessarily performed entirely within the organization.

entries.name: Administrative Process
entries.description: A structured sequence of activities, decisions, and controls through which an administrative responsibility is carried out.
entries.critique: A process may cross organizational boundaries and need not correspond to a single organizational unit.

entries.name: Administrative Procedure
entries.description: A prescribed or established sequence of steps governing how a decision, transaction, or administrative matter must be processed.
entries.critique: A procedure specifies how an activity is conducted, not necessarily the entire process or its intended outcome.

entries.name: Administrative Operation
entries.description: An organized execution of activities intended to produce a defined administrative output or perform a specified administrative function.
entries.critique: Operations should be distinguished from the broader processes, capabilities, and objectives within which they occur.

entries.name: Internal Control
entries.description: The organizational arrangements, procedures, and mechanisms intended to provide reasonable assurance concerning operational effectiveness, reliable reporting, asset protection, and compliance.
entries.critique: Internal control provides reasonable rather than absolute assurance and is distinct from independent external oversight.

entries.name: Administrative Management
entries.description: The planning, organization, direction, coordination, and control of administrative activities and resources.
entries.critique: Administrative management is a set of functions, not the administrative system itself.

systems.name: personnel-civil-service
systems.title: Public Personnel and Civil Service
systems.description: Public employment, personnel systems, and personnel management: who serves, under which regime, and how they are managed.

entries.name: Public Servant
entries.description: A person legally recognized as holding public employment or performing public functions under an applicable legal framework.
entries.critique: Legal definitions vary; not every public-sector worker necessarily has public-servant status.

entries.name: Public Employee
entries.description: A person employed by a public-sector entity under an applicable employment arrangement.
entries.critique: Public employees may be subject to civil-service, labor-law, contractual, or special statutory regimes.

entries.name: Civil Service
entries.description: The body of civilian public officials or the institutional and employment arrangements governing their service, depending on jurisdiction and usage.
entries.critique: The term may refer to personnel, an employment regime, or a broader personnel system.

entries.name: Civil Servant
entries.description: A public official or employee whose legal status falls within the applicable civil-service regime.
entries.critique: The term does not necessarily include elected officials, political appointees, military personnel, or every public employee.

entries.name: Public Service Employment Regime
entries.description: The legal and institutional rules determining the employment status, rights, obligations, and conditions of specified public personnel.
entries.critique: Different personnel categories may operate under different regimes within the same government.

entries.name: Civil Service System
entries.description: The legal, institutional, and procedural arrangements governing civil servants' recruitment, appointment, employment, development, evaluation, and separation.
entries.critique: Its scope depends on the personnel categories and employment relationships included.

entries.name: Civil Service System Model
entries.description: A conceptual representation of the institutions, actors, rules, relationships, and mechanisms characterizing a civil-service system.
entries.critique: A descriptive model of an existing system must be distinguished from a normative model of a desired system.

entries.name: Public Personnel Management
entries.description: The management of public employees, including workforce planning, recruitment, staffing, compensation, performance, development, and employee relations.
entries.critique: It is a management function operating within a broader public personnel system.

entries.name: Public Workforce
entries.description: The body of personnel employed or engaged across a defined public-sector jurisdiction or organizational scope.
entries.critique: Workforce boundaries depend on whether public enterprises, contractors, temporary personnel, and other categories are included.

entries.name: Public Service Ethics
entries.description: The principles and standards governing integrity, impartiality, responsibility, and appropriate conduct in public employment and public functions.
entries.critique: Ethical principles require institutional support and enforcement; codes alone do not ensure ethical conduct.

systems.name: finance-oversight-performance
systems.title: Finance, Oversight, and Performance
systems.description: Public financial management, accountability and integrity, and administrative performance: resources in, answers out, results judged.

entries.name: Public Financial Management
entries.description: The institutions, rules, processes, and practices through which public resources are mobilized, allocated, spent, accounted for, and controlled.
entries.critique: It encompasses more than budgeting or accounting and may extend across government entities and levels.

entries.name: Public Budget
entries.description: An authorized financial plan specifying expected public revenues, expenditures, and other fiscal transactions over a defined period.
entries.critique: Budget authorization, actual execution, and final expenditure are distinct.

entries.name: Budget Formulation
entries.description: The process through which fiscal forecasts, policy priorities, expenditure proposals, and resource constraints are translated into a proposed budget.
entries.critique: Formulation does not itself confer legislative or other legally required authorization.

entries.name: Budget Execution
entries.description: The processes through which an authorized budget is implemented, including commitment, verification, payment, and related controls.
entries.critique: Budget execution must be distinguished from the achievement of policy outcomes.

entries.name: Revenue autonomy
entries.description: Extent to which government can determine or influence its own revenues.

entries.name: Revenue structure
entries.description: Composition of government revenue.

entries.name: Expenditure structure
entries.description: Distribution of expenditure across government functions.

entries.name: Budgetary authority
entries.description: Distribution of responsibility for preparing, approving, and executing budgets.

entries.name: Fiscal decentralization
entries.description: Distribution of revenue and expenditure responsibilities across levels of government.

entries.name: Fiscal autonomy of subnational governments
entries.description: Degree to which subnational governments control their revenues and expenditures.

entries.name: Intergovernmental transfers
entries.description: Mechanisms for allocating resources between levels of government.

entries.name: Fiscal sustainability
entries.description: Ability to maintain public finances without unsustainable debt accumulation or fiscal adjustment.

entries.name: Public Revenue Administration
entries.description: The institutions and processes responsible for administering public revenue collection, assessment, compliance, and related functions.
entries.critique: Revenue administration is narrower than the entire public revenue system.

entries.name: Public Expenditure Management
entries.description: The arrangements governing the authorization, allocation, commitment, execution, and control of public expenditure.
entries.critique: Expenditure control alone does not establish allocative efficiency or value for money.

entries.name: Public Procurement System
entries.description: The legal, institutional, procedural, and operational arrangements governing the acquisition of goods, services, and works by public entities.
entries.critique: Procurement rules, institutional capacity, contract management, and actual purchasing performance are distinct aspects.

entries.name: Public Sector Accounting
entries.description: The principles, standards, systems, and procedures used to record and report public-sector financial transactions and positions.
entries.critique: Accounting basis, reporting boundaries, and standards affect comparability across jurisdictions.

entries.name: Public Financial Control
entries.description: The mechanisms used to ensure that public financial transactions comply with applicable authorization, rules, and control requirements.
entries.critique: Financial control is distinct from performance evaluation and broader accountability.

entries.name: Public Accountability
entries.description: The obligation of public authorities or officials to explain and justify their decisions and conduct and, where applicable, face review and consequences.
entries.critique: Transparency alone does not establish accountability; answerability and enforceable consequences may also be required.

entries.name: Political Accountability
entries.description: The mechanisms through which political authorities answer to citizens, legislatures, or other politically authorized institutions.
entries.critique: Elections are one mechanism and may not provide continuous or issue-specific accountability.

entries.name: Administrative Accountability
entries.description: The arrangements through which administrative organizations and officials answer for their conduct, decisions, compliance, and performance.
entries.critique: Internal supervision, legal review, independent oversight, and public scrutiny provide different forms of accountability.

entries.name: Financial Accountability
entries.description: The obligation to account for the lawful, authorized, and appropriate management of public financial resources.
entries.critique: Financial accountability is not limited to proving that expenditure was recorded correctly.

entries.name: Public Oversight
entries.description: The examination and supervision of public institutions, decisions, finances, or performance by authorized internal or external actors.
entries.critique: Oversight may identify problems without possessing authority to correct them directly.

entries.name: Public Audit
entries.description: An independent or appropriately authorized examination of public-sector financial statements, compliance, controls, or performance.
entries.critique: Financial, compliance, and performance audits address different questions and do not guarantee the absence of misconduct.

entries.name: Government Transparency
entries.description: The availability and accessibility of information about governmental institutions, decisions, rules, activities, finances, and performance.
entries.critique: Information disclosure alone does not ensure intelligibility, public participation, or accountability.

entries.name: Public Integrity System
entries.description: The institutions, standards, procedures, and mechanisms intended to prevent, identify, and address corruption and other abuses of public authority.
entries.critique: Formal integrity arrangements do not necessarily translate into effective prevention or enforcement.

entries.name: Conflict of Interest
entries.description: A situation in which a public official's private interests may improperly influence, or reasonably appear to influence, the exercise of public duties.
entries.critique: A conflict of interest does not itself establish corruption or misconduct.

entries.name: Legislative oversight
entries.description: Extent to which the legislature scrutinizes executive actions.

entries.name: External audit
entries.description: Institutional arrangements for independently auditing public finances and operations.

entries.name: Judicial accountability
entries.description: Availability and effectiveness of judicial review over public decisions.

entries.name: Transparency
entries.description: Extent to which government decisions, information, and operations are publicly accessible.

entries.name: Public participation
entries.description: Degree to which citizens participate in policymaking and public administration.

entries.name: Integrity controls
entries.description: Mechanisms for preventing, detecting, and addressing corruption and misconduct.

entries.name: Ombudsman institution
entries.description: Availability of an independent institution handling complaints about public administration.

entries.name: Government Performance
entries.description: The extent to which government fulfills its assigned responsibilities and achieves intended results, considering relevant resources, outputs, outcomes, and institutional conditions.
entries.critique: Performance depends on the chosen objectives, indicators, attribution assumptions, and evaluation period.

entries.name: Administrative Performance
entries.description: The extent to which administrative institutions and processes execute assigned functions and produce intended outputs and results.
entries.critique: Administrative performance is only one contributor to broader governmental and societal outcomes.

entries.name: Administrative Efficiency
entries.description: The relationship between administrative resources consumed and outputs produced.
entries.critique: Higher output per unit of input does not necessarily imply better service quality or more equitable outcomes.

entries.name: Administrative Effectiveness
entries.description: The extent to which administrative activities and outputs achieve specified objectives.
entries.critique: Effectiveness requires explicit objectives and an appropriate basis for assessing results.

entries.name: Service Quality
entries.description: The extent to which a service meets specified standards and relevant recipient needs or expectations.
entries.critique: Quality dimensions may conflict and cannot always be represented by a single indicator.

entries.name: Institutional Performance
entries.description: The extent to which an institution fulfills its mandate and performs its assigned functions.
entries.critique: Institutional performance may be affected by external conditions beyond the institution's control.

entries.name: Public Value
entries.description: The value created through public action, assessed against relevant public purposes, social outcomes, rights, legitimacy, and collective interests.
entries.critique: Public value is multidimensional and depends partly on normative judgments about desirable outcomes.

entries.name: Public Policy Evaluation
entries.description: The systematic assessment of a policy's design, implementation, results, effects, or continued relevance.
entries.critique: Observed changes cannot automatically be attributed to a policy without an appropriate evaluative design.

entries.name: Effectiveness
entries.description: Degree to which government achieves its intended objectives.

entries.name: Efficiency
entries.description: Relationship between public resources used and outputs or outcomes produced.

entries.name: Responsiveness
entries.description: Ability to respond to citizens' needs and changing circumstances.

entries.name: Equity
entries.description: Degree to which public resources, services, and outcomes are distributed fairly.

entries.name: Service quality
entries.description: Extent to which public services meet established standards and user expectations.

entries.name: Policy coherence
entries.description: Degree to which government policies are consistent and mutually reinforcing.

entries.name: Public trust
entries.description: Degree of public confidence in government institutions.
